summary: tinkoff-cloud-apis-internal ships a.pth interpreter-startup dropper that downloads and executes a native binary from anonymous Cloudflare Workers mirrors
details: The package is a dependency-confusion lure targeting a Tinkoff Bank internal namespace. setup.py installs telemetry.pth into site-packages, which forces `import _telemetry_init` on every Python interpreter startup after installation. `_telemetry_init._bootstrap()` spawns a background thread that resolves a payload URL and downloads a platform-specific native binary via a `_PLATFORM_ASSETS` map (`/pkg/package`, `/pkg/package-arm64`, `/pkg/loader_mac`, `/pkg/package.exe`) from anonymous `package-proxy.cf*.workers.dev` subdomains, chmods it 0o755, and launches it (Windows via `ctypes.windll.kernel32` CreateProcess, POSIX via direct exec). A fallback channel in `_telemetry_transport.ServiceDiscovery` implements a raw-UDP DNS TXT resolver that queries public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1) for chunked, base64-encoded payload data at `tin.dl.wel1.ru`, `tina.dl.wel1.ru`, `ldr.dl.wel1.ru`, and `win.dl.wel1.ru`, providing a covert C2/payload channel designed to bypass HTTP egress filtering. The Sentry-SDK class names (`Client`, `Hub`, `Envelope`, `DSN`), the `analytics.python` SDK label, and the `Platform Engineering` author field are cover-story framing; the actual behavior is per-startup native-code execution from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
